games.title: Then and Now Town
games.skillName: How land use and settlements change over time
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to describe and understand key aspects of human geography, including: types of settlement and land use; name and locate counties and cities of the United Kingdom, geographical regions and their identifying human and physical characteristics, key topographical features (including hills, mountains, coasts and rivers), and land-use patterns; and understand how some of these aspects have changed over time
games.instruction: Think about how places change, then tap the best answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about what people need from the land, then try again.

questions.ask: Hundreds of years ago, where did most people in Britain live?
In the Industrial Revolution, many people moved from farms to where?
Why were many early settlements built next to rivers?
Why did many villages grow into towns around a market?
A tiny settlement of a few houses, with no shop or church, is called a what?
When a town grows bigger, what often happens to the fields around it?
Many old coal mines in Britain have closed. What has some of that land become?
An old factory is turned into flats. What has changed?
What do we call land used for growing crops and keeping animals?
Land covered mostly by people's homes is called what kind of land use?
